html:
The Narragansett are an Algonquian people of Rhode Island, living west of Narragansett Bay. In the early 1600s they were the strongest people of southern New England.

They farmed maize, beans and squash, fished and gathered shellfish, and made wampum, shell beads used in trade and diplomacy. The epidemic of 1616 to 1619 that emptied the coast to the east largely spared them, so they took tribute from weakened neighbours like the Wampanoag.

In 1636 the sachems Canonicus and Miantonomi let Roger Williams, banished from Massachusetts, settle at Providence. He learned their language and wrote a book on it in 1643. They sided with the English in the Pequot War but were later rivals of the Mohegan. In December 1675, during King Philip's War, colonial troops attacked their fortified town in the Great Swamp and killed hundreds. The Narragansett Indian Tribe won federal recognition in 1983.
